va-55.cap: VA-55: VTOL rotors on twin booms for take-off and landing, and a fixed wing for cruise.
Exhibition poster: specifications, engineering rationale, business case, concept of operations, regulatory compliance and roadmap.
The image we used to sum up VA-55's key figures.
Requirements compliance matrix, updated for every design iteration. Green: met. Yellow: partly met. Red: not met. Blue: not yet calculated.
General arrangement drawing. The datum sits at the wing leading edge, and the drawing carries custom tolerances and the CoG positions with and without payload.
Tail-to-VTOL-boom interface drawing. A second trade study after PDR moved the cruise motor and changed the layout.
Transport dimensions: every part was checked against the transport van, and the tailplane was redesigned to fit.
Exploded view of the full aircraft.
Benchmark against four quadcopter sprayers and the fixed-wing Pyka Pelican, using their published specifications.
Quick-disconnect joint: titanium adaptors bonded into the carbon-fibre booms take a threaded connector and tightener.
Step-by-step assembly guide for joining the tail and booms on site before each flight.

andel-bundguard.cap: BundGuard variants built from one main body with bolted brackets.
Main body with the probes on a removable sensor card.

andel-products.cap: Gully flood sensor enclosure, redesigned for quick installation with few tools and no specialist staff.
Too big for the SLS printer, so the enclosure was designed for FDM: 45° chamfers under overhangs, break-away support walls and a chosen print orientation.
CellarGuard, redesigned for easier assembly and still compatible with the old mounting.
Panel-drilling jig that standardises hand-machined parts.
FlowStop 2 enclosure: about 20% more compact, with the valve turned horizontal and a contoured base so it only fits the right way round.
Circuitry enclosure adapted for SLS printing: powder drainage, print orientation and warping.
Water-quality sensor: every sensor packed into the tight space of a bollard that moves with the water level.
Bollard changes designed around the supplier's limited tooling.
Sensor housing, with approximate sizes for PCBs and connectors that were not yet designed.
My placement poster: one page covering my work on four Andel products.

chargepoint.cap: Sensor box, first versions: 150 mm, 200 mm and single-sensor boxes.
Final sensor box: re-orienting the open/closed sensors onto one plane halved its size.
316 stainless steel test frame for a 100 kg product on an IBC.
The frame in use: it fitted the IBC and held the full 100 kg load.
Valve lifting points: the handles were confirmed as safe lifting points with a large margin.
Eyebolt handle variant: one eyebolt can carry more than the heaviest valve.
Spring and sealed spring cover, designed with the ChargeBag (plastics) engineers.
Bracket that fits a vibratory piston to the PuroGrab holder.

tailfin.cap: Brief: an adjustable version of Tailfin's AeroPack seat-post-to-pack connector.
Product design specification (part 1): function, mounting, strength.
Product design specification (part 2): manufacture and user experience.
Concept selection: each concept scored against the datum (Concept 5) on every criterion.
Concepts 4 and 6 scored highest, so both became final designs.
Final design, Concept 4: a 128 g tool-less aluminium connector with ±90° of motion at the seat post and 180° at the pack bracket.
Final design, Concept 6: a lower-cost connector whose length is set through ratcheted holes.

wing-design.cap: Mass-optimised wing panel; the code generated this final model automatically.
Flowchart of the script sequence that produced the final design.
Reserve factors as the stiffener width changes. A design passed only when every reserve factor was above 1.
Mass and thickness against stiffener width.
Skin laminate stacking sequence, chosen by my function following industry laminate rules.
The laminate design is 25% lighter per unit area than the aluminium panel.
